title: The Day the Mona Lisa Vanished—and the Musical It Inspired
summary: Have you ever lost something really important, like your favorite toy or a homework assignment? Imagine losing the most famous painting in the world! That's what happened in 1911 when the Mona Lisa disappeared from the Louvre museum in Paris. The thief? An Italian worker named Vincenzo Peruggia, who had helped install a glass case around the painting. He knew exactly how to take it out. On August 21, he dressed like a regular worker, lifted the painting off the wall, and walked out with it hidden under his smock. Nobody noticed for 28 hours! When the museum realized the painting was gone, they panicked. They even questioned famous artists like Pablo Picasso. But Peruggia kept the Mona Lisa in a trunk in his apartment for two years. Then he tried to sell it back to an art dealer in Italy, claiming he wanted to return it to its home country. He was caught, but many Italians saw him as a hero. The theft made the Mona Lisa a superstar. Before it was stolen, it wasn't even the most famous painting in its own gallery. Now, composer Andrew Lloyd Webber—the guy behind The Phantom of the Opera and Cats—is turning this crazy true story into a musical. He says it's about how the painting disappeared and ended up in Italy. With his love for big, dramatic shows, this could be a spectacle worth waiting in line for!
why_it_matters: Sometimes a single event can turn something ordinary into a legend — just like a mistake or a mystery can make a story unforgettable, showing how history is full of surprises.

background_read: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci (the famous Italian artist and inventor from the Renaissance) around 1503.
Before the theft, the painting was not as famous worldwide — the news of its disappearance made it a global sensation.
Andrew Lloyd Webber (the British composer behind The Phantom of the Opera and Cats) loves turning dramatic true stories into spectacular musicals.

perspectives.description: Peruggia was seen as a hero in Italy, who wanted to bring a masterpiece back to its homeland.
The theft was a crime that put a priceless artwork at risk and caused panic at the museum.
The theft accidentally boosted the Mona Lisa's fame, turning it into the most famous painting in the world and inspiring new art like an upcoming musical.
